speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for coming in. I see you are experiencing shortness of breath, increased abdominal girth, and a large ovarian mass. To better understand your condition, have you noticed any pain in your abdomen or pelvis, and have you experienced any changes in your bowel or bladder habits?

speaker: Patient
text: 40-year-old nulliparous woman. The patient reports experiencing shortness of breath and noticeable increase in abdominal size over the past month. She denies any significant medical history, previous surgeries, or use of medications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given your age, lack of pregnancy history, and the presence of a large ovarian mass causing shortness of breath and abdominal distension, I need to assess if the mass has spread. Do you have a history of endometriosis or any previous unexplained fluid retention? REQUEST TEST: CA-125; REQUEST TEST: CT Abdomen and Pelvis.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Shortness of breath. I also have Increased abdominal girth, Fatigue, No significant weight loss or gain. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Pyelonephritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is an unusual suggestion for pyelonephritis given your ovarian mass; did the mass cause urinary obstruction, or do you have any pain when urinating? REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis; REQUEST IMAGES: CT Abdomen and Pelvis.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Ovarian Malignancy (likely Advanced Stage)

The CT confirms a complex ovarian mass causing ascites, pleural effusion (respiratory distress), and ureteral obstruction (hydronephrosis), effectively ruling out pyelonephritis given the sterile urinalysis. This clinical picture is highly suggestive of an advanced ovarian cancer.
